answer_text:
We need \(28! \pmod{799}\). Factor the modulus:

\[
799=17\cdot 47.
\]

We compute \(28!\) modulo \(17\) and modulo \(47\), then combine with the Chinese remainder theorem.

### Modulo \(17\)

Since \(28!\) contains the factor \(17\),

\[
28! \equiv 0 \pmod{17}.
\]

### Modulo \(47\)

Wilson’s theorem gives

\[
46! \equiv -1 \pmod{47}.
\]

Split \(46!\) as

\[
46! = 28! \cdot (29\cdot 30 \cdots 46).
\]

Modulo \(47\),

\[
29,30,\dots,46 \equiv -18,-17,\dots,-1 \pmod{47}.
\]

There are \(18\) signs, so

\[
29\cdot 30 \cdots 46 \equiv 18! \pmod{47}.
\]

Thus

\[
28! \cdot 18! \equiv -1 \pmod{47}.
\]

Now compute \(18! \pmod{47}\):

\[
1\cdot 2\cdots 9 \equiv 40 \pmod{47},
\]
\[
10\cdot 11\cdots 18 \equiv 34 \pmod{47}.
\]

So

\[
18! \equiv 40\cdot 34 \equiv 44 \equiv -3 \pmod{47}.
\]

Hence

\[
28! \cdot (-3) \equiv -1 \pmod{47}.
\]

Since \(3^{-1}\equiv 16\pmod{47}\),

\[
28! \equiv 16 \pmod{47}.
\]

Now solve

\[
x \equiv 0 \pmod{17},\qquad x \equiv 16 \pmod{47}.
\]

Let \(x=17k\). Then

\[
17k \equiv 16 \pmod{47}.
\]

Since \(17^{-1}\equiv 36 \pmod{47}\),

\[
k \equiv 16\cdot 36 \equiv 12 \pmod{47}.
\]

Thus

\[
x \equiv 17\cdot 12 = 204 \pmod{799}.
\]

\[
\boxed{204}
\]
